rubrics.evidence: The patch adds `resolve_input_datasets` to `tensorrec/input_utils.py` and `tensorrec.py` imports `create_tensorrec_iterator`, `get_dimensions_from_tensorrec_dataset`, and `resolve_input_datasets as _resolve_input_datasets` from `.input_utils`. The model now uses those owners: `_build_input_iterators` calls `create_tensorrec_iterator(...)`, fit uses `get_dimensions_from_tensorrec_dataset(...)`, and `TensorRec.resolve_input_datasets` only delegates via `return _resolve_input_datasets(raw_input)`. The model's private `_create_input_iterator`, `_create_dataset_from_sparse_matrix`, `_create_dataset_from_tfrecord`, and `_get_dataset_dimensions` implementations are deleted, so the input/dataset preparation logic lives in the input/utility area rather than as copies on the model.
rubrics.criterion: Input/dataset preparation responsibilities — raw-input resolution for the accepted input forms, sparse-matrix-to-Dataset and TFRecord-to-Dataset conversion, iterator construction, and dataset dimension probing — are implemented outside the model class in the package's input/utility area, and the model class declares no copies of that preparation logic.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch restores the metric bodies in eval.py: _setup_ndcg/_idcg/_dcg, precision_at_k, recall_at_k, ndcg_at_k, and f1_score_at_k are implemented with numpy/scipy, and eval_random_ranks_on_dataset calls those local functions. The top-level `from .tensorrec import TensorRec` is removed; TensorRec is imported only lazily in grid_check_model_on_dataset to instantiate models. In tensorrec.py, the model's _setup_ndcg/_idcg/_dcg bodies are deleted and precision_at_k/recall_at_k/ndcg_at_k/f1_score_at_k are reduced to delegations to imported eval functions, leaving no rank-metric arithmetic in the model class.
rubrics.criterion: The rank-evaluation arithmetic (precision/recall/NDCG/F1 over predicted ranks, including the NDCG sub-steps) is computed by the evaluation module itself or by a cohesive non-model helper it imports, and the model class declares no rank-metric math; the evaluation module no longer imports the high-level model to obtain metric values.

rubrics.evidence: The request says session ownership belongs with the session helpers "not as a forwarder, but actually owning it" and model call sites should consume those owners. The agent patch restores ownership in session_management.py (`_tf_session` global with `get_session`/`set_session`), but tensorrec.py still declares `@classmethod get_session` returning `_get_session()` and `@classmethod set_session` calling `_set_session(session)`, and leaves internal call sites using `self.get_session()`/`cls.get_session()` (e.g., predict/save/load). Thus the model class still declares session accessor classmethods and model code reaches the session through them rather than directly through the session-management owner.
rubrics.criterion: Shared TensorFlow session state and its get/set accessors are owned by the session-management module rather than the model class: the model class holds no session attribute and declares no session accessor classmethods, and model code obtains the session through the session-management owner.

rubrics.evidence: The agent removed the in-class copies `_sample_item_indices` and `_calculate_batched_alpha` from TensorRec (deleted in tensorrec.py diff) and imported the shared utility implementations: `from .util import calculate_batched_alpha, sample_items`. The fitting internals now call these utilities directly: `_build_tf_graph` uses `partial(sample_items, replace=...)` and the fit feed dict uses `calculate_batched_alpha(num_batches=len(initializer_sets), alpha=alpha)`. Both `sample_items` and `calculate_batched_alpha` remain defined in `tensorrec/util.py`, satisfying the requirement that the training-auxiliary math is provided by the shared utility area and consumed by the model's fitting internals.
rubrics.criterion: The training-auxiliary math (stochastic item sampling for sampled losses and the batched regularization scaling) is provided by the shared utility area, not by in-class copies; the model's fitting internals import or call the utility implementations.

rubrics.evidence: The patch distributes the re-homed stages across cohesive owners instead of one catch-all: eval.py restores local metric implementations (_setup_ndcg, _idcg, _dcg, precision_at_k, recall_at_k, ndcg_at_k, f1_score_at_k) and drops the top-level TensorRec import; session_management.py owns _tf_session with get_session/set_session; input_utils.py adds resolve_input_datasets; util.py keeps sample_items/calculate_batched_alpha. In tensorrec.py the private copies are removed and TensorRec.get_session/set_session/resolve_input_datasets/precision_at_k/etc. become thin delegators, so no single class holds input preparation, metrics, and session handling implementations together.
rubrics.criterion: The absorbed areas are not simply re-parked in a second catch-all owner: no single new or existing class ends up holding several of the re-homed responsibility stages (e.g., an omnibus helper object carrying input preparation, metrics, and session handling together).

rubrics.evidence: All model-lifecycle call sites are rewired to the restored owners: _build_input_iterators calls create_tensorrec_iterator from input_utils with unchanged shared names ('tf_user_feature_iterator', 'tf_item_feature_iterator', 'tf_interaction_iterator'); _build_tf_graph uses util.sample_items; _fit uses get_dimensions_from_tensorrec_dataset and calculate_batched_alpha from input_utils/util; _create_batched_dataset_initializers calls self.resolve_input_datasets which delegates to input_utils.resolve_input_datasets; predict/predict_rank/predict_similar_items/representation/bias and save_model/load_model all use self.get_session()/cls.get_session() which delegate to session_management; fit_and_evaluate and the static metric methods call eval module functions (eval_precision_at_k, etc.). The in-class copies (_create_input_iterator, _get_dataset_dimensions, _sample_item_indices, _calculate_batched_alpha, _setup_ndcg/_idcg/_dcg, tf_session) are removed with no stale references, and graph hook attr/node name dicts are untouched.
rubrics.criterion: All internal callers are rewired: the model's graph-building, fitting, prediction, and save/load call sites consume the restored owners instead of the removed in-class copies, with the iterator shared names and graph hook names unchanged so previously saved models still restore.

rubrics.evidence: In eval.py, eval_random_ranks_on_dataset now calls the module-level eval functions directly: precision_at_k(random_guesses, interactions, k=precision_k), recall_at_k(...), and ndcg_at_k(...) instead of the smell's TensorRec.precision_at_k/recall_at_k/ndcg_at_k calls. For grid_check_model_on_dataset, the grid search calls model.fit_and_evaluate(...), and in tensorrec.py fit_and_evaluate now computes metrics via the imported eval owners: eval_precision_at_k, eval_recall_at_k, and eval_ndcg_at_k (imported from .eval as eval_f1_score_at_k, eval_ndcg_at_k, eval_precision_at_k, eval_recall_at_k) rather than TensorRec.precision_at_k etc. Both dataset-level routines thus route metric computation through the restored eval-module owners, not model-class metric methods.
rubrics.criterion: The dataset-level evaluation routines (the component/epoch grid search over the model and the random-rank baseline scoring) compute their metrics through the restored evaluation owners rather than through model-class methods.

rubrics.evidence: In the agent patch, session_management.py no longer contains any in-body `from .tensorrec import TensorRec`; instead it has module-level `import tensorflow as tf` and a module-level `_tf_session = None`, with get_session()/set_session() operating on that global. tensorrec.py imports these helpers at module level (`from .session_management import get_session as _get_session, set_session as _set_session`), so session access resolves through normal imports without a call-time model import.
rubrics.criterion: No support module needs a call-time (in-function-body) import of the model class to perform its own job; session access in the session-management module resolves through normal module-level imports without breaking package import order.

rubrics.evidence: In tensorrec.py the agent deletes the absorbed in-class duplicates: `_create_input_iterator`, `_create_dataset_from_sparse_matrix`, `_create_dataset_from_tfrecord`, `_get_dataset_dimensions`, `_sample_item_indices`, `_calculate_batched_alpha`, `_setup_ndcg`, `_idcg`, and `_dcg` are removed, and the `tf_session` class attribute is removed. `get_session`/`set_session` now delegate to `session_management`, `resolve_input_datasets` delegates to `input_utils.resolve_input_datasets`, and `precision_at_k`/`recall_at_k`/`ndcg_at_k`/`f1_score_at_k` bodies are replaced with `return eval_*` calls. The remaining `fit_and_evaluate` is a thin public convenience that calls the restored `eval` metric functions, so no dead or unreachable private duplicate members remain alongside the restored owners.
rubrics.criterion: No orphaned residue of the consolidation remains: the in-class duplicates absorbed during the accumulation (input preparation, sampling/scaling math, metric bodies, session members) are deleted from the model class rather than left alongside the restored owners as dead or unreachable private members. A thin fit-then-score orchestration kept on the class as a public convenience is acceptable only if every absorbed implementation it needs lives with the restored owners.

rubrics.evidence: tensorrec/util.py keeps `import tensorflow as tf` and `from .input_utils import create_tensorrec_dataset_from_sparse_matrix, resolve_input_datasets`, but the rewritten `datasets_from_raw_input` now only calls `resolve_input_datasets(raw_input)`; the shown body no longer references `tf` or `create_tensorrec_dataset_from_sparse_matrix`, leaving those imports unused. rubrics.criterion: Module imports match what the modules actually use after the repair: imports that existed only to serve the absorbed bodies (for example the arithmetic and six-compatibility imports the model module gained) are removed when their consumers are removed, and no new unused imports are introduced.

rubrics.evidence: Evaluation functions stay in tensorrec/eval.py with unchanged names/signatures/defaults (e.g., precision_at_k(predicted_ranks, test_interactions, k=10, preserve_rows=False), recall_at_k, ndcg_at_k, f1_score_at_k, fit_and_eval, grid_check_model_on_dataset, eval_random_ranks_on_dataset); the top-level TensorRec import is removed and only lazily imported in grid_check_model_on_dataset. rubrics.criterion: The public compatibility surface is intact: the evaluation functions, the session helpers, and the input/utility functions remain importable from their existing module paths with their pre-existing names, signatures, and default arguments.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch restores session ownership to tensorrec/session_management.py via a module-level _tf_session global with get_session()/set_session(), and TensorRec.get_session/set_session become thin delegates to _get_session/_set_session. _build_input_iterators keeps the original internal iterator names via create_tensorrec_iterator(name='tf_user_feature_iterator'/'tf_item_feature_iterator'/'tf_interaction_iterator'), so the save/load/reset session wiring and iterator/graph names are preserved rather than renamed or re-bound.
rubrics.criterion: Persistence round trips still behave identically: a model saved before or after the repair loads after a session reset, and its predictions and ranks equal those of the in-memory model it was saved from.

rubrics.evidence: session_management.py now owns the shared session via a module-level `_tf_session = None`; get_session() builds/returns that single global session, and set_session(None) resets `_tf_session = None` so the next get_session() creates a fresh tf.Session(). tensorrec.py imports `get_session as _get_session, set_session as _set_session` from session_management and makes TensorRec.get_session()/set_session() delegate to those helpers; the model class no longer stores its own `tf_session`, and internal call sites use self.get_session()/cls.get_session(), preserving one shared session across model and module-level users.
rubrics.criterion: Session semantics are preserved: the whole package still observes one shared session (model code and module-level session users included), and requesting a session reset by passing None to the session setter forces a fresh session at the next use.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch leaves eval.py's module-level fit_and_eval unchanged: the hunk at def fit_and_eval only adds a lazy import to grid_check_model_on_dataset and does not restore its body, so fit_and_eval remains the smell's one-line pass-through return model.fit_and_evaluate(...), an upward delegate into a model-class member.
rubrics.criterion: The evaluation module functions are not left as upward delegates: no module-level evaluation function is implemented as a pass-through call into model-class members, even if the bodies were otherwise moved.

rubrics.evidence: The refactor request requires end-to-end model behavior not to change. agent.patch keeps the error imports (`ModelNotBiasedException, ModelNotFitException, ModelWithoutAttentionException, BatchNonSparseInputException`) and does not alter the prediction-method guard clauses or `_create_batched_dataset_initializers` validation; it only rewires session/dataset/metric calls to `session_management.get_session`, `input_utils.resolve_input_datasets`, and `eval` functions, so the same guards remain load-bearing.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not break the not-yet-fit / not-biased guards or batched-input validation: predicting without fitting, using biased outputs on an unbiased model, attention-representation access on a non-attention model, and mis-shaped batched fitting still raise the same errors as before.
